negative_findings.description: No Serbian-language (sr) job portal, complaint channel or event listing specific to Kosovo/XK was found. Serbian-language searches ('posao Kosovo banka platne kartice specijalista konkurs oglas') returned almost exclusively Serbia, Bosnia and Montenegro employers (Infostud, NLB RS, Addiko, Erste, Adriatic Bank) with no Kosovo-domiciled institution.
negative_findings.result_summary: sr-language querying produced a usable role glossary (platne kartice, bankomat, oglas za posao, konkurs, specijalista) but zero Kosovo-specific indirect sources.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The sr-speaking north-Kosovo banking segment is a real market slice; if its hiring, complaint and event signals exist they are not discoverable via mainstream sr job boards, so the cell currently has an sr blind spot.

negative_findings.description: No independent web domain for Shoqata e Bankave te Kosoves (Kosovo Banking Association) was surfaced. The only reachable descriptions of the association sit on a member bank's page and on the Albanian Association of Banks site.
negative_findings.result_summary: Association confirmed to exist and to co-organise sector fora (e.g. an October 2023 cybersecurity-in-banking forum with AAB Albania), but no own events/agenda page was located.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A banking association's conference agendas and member statistics are one of the richest indirect channels; without its own domain the cell must reconstruct its activity from member-bank and partner-association pages, losing timeliness.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated Kosovo financial ombudsman institution or standalone banking-ombudsman complaint-statistics publication was identified. Complaint handling appears to sit inside BQK's Divizioni i Ankesave te Shfrytezuesve te Sherbimeve Financiare rather than an independent ombudsman.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches in sq surfaced the BQK complaints division and portal (ankesat.bqk-kos.org) and the general consumer-protection legal framework, but no separate ombudsman body publishing card/ATM complaint series.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cell's rationale assumed an ombudsman data stream; in XK that stream is regulator-internal, so complaint statistics are only as granular as BQK's annual report chooses to be.

negative_findings.description: No recurring Kosovo-specific payments or cards conference (with a published agenda and speaker list) was found. Payments content appears only as sessions inside broader events: the BQK regional crypto/digital-money conference, KosICT, and the region-wide Balkan Payment Forum.
negative_findings.result_summary: No 'Kosovo Payments Summit' style standing event located in sq or en searching.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Conference-slide leakage of transaction volumes is a core mechanism for this cell; with no national payments conference, the cell must lean on regional events and regulator conferences, which are less XK-specific.

negative_findings.description: LinkedIn content for Kosovo payment executives is behind login and its terms restrict automated collection; The Banker and Euromoney award citations are behind paywalls.
negative_findings.result_summary: Named executive signals were only partially visible via search snippets (e.g. a Head of Cards and POS Business at TEB; a Head of Retail Banking Group at BKT Kosova; a new Head of Channel Management at ProCredit Bank Kosova).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The two highest-yield indirect channels for this cell (executive posts, award citations) are the two most access-constrained, pushing the collection design toward manual/licensed rather than automated methods.

negative_findings.description: No URL in this slice was fetched or liveness-checked; all URLs come from search-result metadata and snippets.
negative_findings.result_summary: Candidates are recorded with confidence scores only; paywall/login flags on thebanker.com, euromoney.com and linkedin.com are hypotheses, not observed HTTP verdicts.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The downstream deterministic verification pass must resolve these before any source is treated as reachable or dead.

coverage_gaps.description: Serbian-language indirect channels for Kosovo (north-Kosovo bank branches, sr-language local media, sr job listings) are effectively uncovered.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run targeted sr searches against known north-Kosovo media domains (e.g. kossev, kim radio) and against Serbian bank groups' career pages for Kosovo locations; build an sr actor map of institutions operating in Serb-majority municipalities.

coverage_gaps.description: Vendor-side weak signals are untouched: processor/switch/ATM-vendor press releases and case studies (card management, POS acquiring, ATM fleets) naming Kosovo banks as customers.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search vendor domains (switch/card-management, ATM manufacturers, POS terminal vendors, regional processors) for Kosovo bank references and case studies; snowball from the platform names that appear in the job ads collected via KosovaJob.

coverage_gaps.description: Cash-usage weak signals (cash-in-transit tenders, ATM cash-replenishment procurement, coin/banknote handling contracts) were not searched in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Query the Kosovo public procurement platform (e-prokurimi) and bank tender notices in sq for ATM servicing, cash transport and terminal supply lots, which reveal ATM fleet size and cash intensity.

coverage_gaps.description: Job ads and conference agendas expire and are frequently removed, so the channel has no retrospective depth unless snapshotted at first sight.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Stand up a first-sight archiving step (and check web.archive.org coverage for kosovajob.com and stikk.org) so the vacancy and agenda series can be back-filled and trended.

coverage_gaps.description: Consumer-side complaint aggregators outside the regulator (consumer associations, the Ministry of Industry/Trade consumer-protection inspectorate, social-media complaint clusters) are unmapped.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Identify Kosovo consumer-protection associations and the ministry inspectorate's reporting, and check whether they disaggregate financial-service complaints in a way BQK does not.

brief: Kosovo's weak-signal layer is real but thin and asymmetric. The strongest, most automatable channel is Albanian-language job advertising — KosovaJob and its network carry dated bank vacancies for card operations, payment-systems support and payments departments that name internal units and platforms — followed by BQK's own oblique outputs: the complaints division and portal, the board-decision notices that record licensing and disciplinary measures, and the annual report's complaint and enforcement tables. Event and award channels exist but are regional rather than national: there is no standing Kosovo payments conference, so agenda leakage must be harvested from the BQK regional conference, KosICT and the Balkan Payment Forum, while The Banker, Global Finance, Euromoney and EBRD award citations supply an annual, externally validated metric drop (partly paywalled). The binding constraints are that the two richest channels — executive LinkedIn activity and award citations — are login- or paywall-gated and therefore need manual or licensed collection, and that Serbian-language coverage for Kosovo is effectively absent, leaving the north-Kosovo segment unobserved.
